subject.title: feat(cron): configurable minimum interval guardrail for recurring jobs

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `cron.minInterval` as the operator-facing cadence guardrail for recurring jobs, with unset/0 preserving current behavior and configured values rejecting or pacing fast schedules?
rationale: This adds a new core config surface and a deliberate configured fail-closed behavior for recurring schedules, which is a product and compatibility choice beyond ordinary code correctness.

options.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail After Fixes
options.body: Keep the core config surface, require docs-map regeneration and rebase/conflict resolution, then merge with the documented opt-in compatibility contract.

options.title: Keep Advisory-Only Direction
options.body: Reject enforcement for now and prefer warning-only behavior like the closed high-frequency schedule variant if configured rejection is too strong.

options.title: Defer Core Config Surface
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers choose a broader cron guardrail policy or a non-core extension point.

recommendation.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail After Fixes
recommendation.body: Keep the core config surface, require docs-map regeneration and rebase/conflict resolution, then merge with the documented opt-in compatibility contract.
